reasoning: Base rates first: TT has beaten its first annual EPS guide 3 of 3 years (+8.3%, +10.5%, +2.0%; FY26 tracking +3.7%) and revenue guides 2 of 3, but the beat is shrinking as the cycle matures, so for FY27 I sit ~2% above the post-print Street ($17.71) and at the whisper ($18.10), not at the historical 8% beat. The Q3 print: revenue +18%, bookings +21%, backlog $12.5B (+73%) but the reaffirmed FY EPS guide implies Q4 $3.45 vs ~$3.59 pre-print Street (~4% cut) with EBITDA margin -40bp and EMEA/APAC margins -250/-390bp; that, not demand, is why the beat sold off -8.6%. Driver build: quarterly Americas/EMEA/APAC revenue and margins calibrated to the filed FY25 and 9M26 segments (base EBIT 3,967.6 vs 3,967.4 reported), backlog >$8B shipping 2027+ supports Americas +11% in FY27, decelerating to +7% in FY28 (lumpy data-center orders). Macro priced by markets: Kalshi 2027 recession 20% (Oct 6; was 38-39% in August on 87.8K contracts), Fed on hold with hike tail; AHRI resi shipments +6.2% YTD; ABI near 50 with inquiries 56.8; hyperscaler capex ~$1trn in 2027 (Moody's). Valuation: NTM P/E is the main leg with the k=0.8 shrink (23.9x -> 22.6x vs 18.3x median; TT's own 10y average trailing P/E 23.1x is a sanity floor for the base). Scenarios: downside (P10 $296) = data-center pause + recession + de-rate to the peer median; upside (P90 $598) = faster backlog conversion and re-rate toward the 5y average. Left tail fatter (sigma 0.33 vs 0.22) because the stock sits on a cyclical backlog peak with a premium multiple. Research was limited to web search/fetch; no option data consulted.

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E 14.2x (LII) to 23.7x (JCI) on 8 whole-company peers; trailing filings EV/EBITDA 11.5x-21.2x (LII, MOD, SPXC, CSW)
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TT NTM P/E 23.9x vs median 18.3x (+31%); exit 22.6x after k = 0.8 shrink. Trailing EV/EBITDA 20.3x vs 17.0x; exit 19.6x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Kept premium (~24% at exit) is what the shrink rule keeps, not argued beyond it: TT has higher segment margins than CARR/LII, 98-100%+ FCF conversion, and a $12.5B backlog (+73%) with >$8B shipping 2027+, which gives more forward visibility than resi-weighted peers. No extra premium beyond the rule.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 8 whole-company peers (CARR, JCI, LII, AAON, MOD, SPXC, CSW, Daikin) plus VRT segment-only; no more genuine listed HVAC OEMs on the same basis (Watsco is a distributor, Comfort Systems a contractor, Midea/Gree excluded as China-domiciled).
